basis: Joint dislocations, skeletal growth abnormalities and hyperlaxity define this congenital glycosylation disorder.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across this heterogeneous duplication group; other organ abnormalities vary by duplicated region.
Congenital iris deficiency with associated ocular malformations and visual impairment; explicitly isolated from systemic disease.
Isolated nail and distal digital soft-tissue abnormalities; no evidence of destructive bone disease or systemic organ involvement.
Nematode infection umbrella with different tissue targets across subtypes; no additional organ consistently affected across the group.
Inherited mitochondrial transport/metabolism disorder umbrella; cardiac, neurologic and blood manifestations differ between subtypes.
Adrenal cortisol excess; myopathy/osteoporosis and persistent skin striae/fragility frequent (30–79%); hypertension and stones are separately coded complications.
Human Newcastle virus infection typically localizes to the conjunctiva; respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish common lasting organ injury.
Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent muscle wasting and foot deformities are common, with pes cavus eventually universal; hearing involvement not established as common.
Ontology grouping class rather than a specific disease; no organ axis applies to the grouping itself.
Nonsyndromic intellectual developmental disorder; no common extra-neurologic organ damage documented.
Premature cranial suture fusion; aortic valve stenosis reported in 1/2 assessed patients supports cardiac involvement, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.
Congenital absence of teeth, sometimes with orofacial clefting; teeth and oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with elevated gonadotropins and reduced ovarian hormones; this is endocrine dysfunction as well as infertility.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; joint hypermobility/brachydactyly and atrial septal defects each 3/3; constipation and hypopigmentation alone do not establish additional organ injury.
Urinary-tract granulomatous inflammation; skin inflammation/ulcers 80–99% in supplied HPO; bowel symptoms alone do not establish common intestinal tissue injury.
Postpartum psychiatric disorder with psychosis and mood symptoms; no intrinsic damage to an organ axis established.
Skeletal dysplasia with abnormal femoral epiphyses, hip deformity and cartilaginous bone lesions.
Congenital anorectal structural defects, including anal stenosis and fistulas; no common additional organ disease specified.
Autoinflammation, arthritis and vasculitis define disease; seizures 3/3 and developmental impairment 2/4; cap excludes anemia (3/4) and renal/skin findings (1/1 assessed).
Inherited ventricular electrical instability causing fibrillation; structural heart disease is not required for cardiovascular classification.
Muscle wasting/deformities usual; optic atrophy and hearing loss are defining features, with exact frequencies unstated; respiratory impairment is variable.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration with visual loss; no extraocular organ involvement established.
Urethral hypospadias 2/3; amblyopia/high hypermetropia and bicuspid aortic valve each 1/2 assessed; minor clinodactyly lacks demonstrated functional injury.
Pathological resorption of external tooth hard tissue; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
